log.title: Towns, throwables, impaling, events
changes: Every town is different now. Each named town has its own layout: a bazaar, a bridge over a chasm, cliff terraces, a walled fort, steaming pools, stilt houses over lava or honey, docks over black water, a bone cathedral, or a village around a giant root or crystal.
Towns also have their own merchants: Gunsmith, Herbalist, Limb-Maker (prosthetics), Armourer, Bombmaker, Outfitter, and a Fence who pays 40% more for what you sell.
Each town has special features: a Hive Shrine, a Hot Spring, a Soup Kitchen, a Bone Dice table, a Cartographer who maps the next three levels, and an Anvil that repairs your armour.

15 new throwables: Throwing Knife, Scrap Star, Javelin, Bola, Poison Dart, Acid Flask, Honey Jar, Spore Pod, Frost Flask, Sticky Charge, Frag Grenade, Flashbang, Smoke Bomb, Incendiary Jar and Clockwork Rattler. Cycle them with T and throw with G. Several are craftable.
Impaling: a heavy thrust or lunge with a spear, knife, machete or similar can run someone through and hold them on the blade. Enemies can do it to you too. Mash SPACE to tear free.
No arms? Left-click kicks and right-click headbutts.
Gore effects are 35% stronger.

10 new random events: Tremors, Flash Flood, Spore Storm, Cold Snap, Heat Bloom, The Hunt, Whispers, Nectar Bloom, Supply Drop and Blood Frenzy. Whatever event is happening shows in a banner at the top of the screen with a countdown.

Level variety: every level picks its own shape from your run's seed — rolling hills, tall chambers, cramped tunnels, pillared halls, rubble fields, big overhangs or terraces — plus random set-pieces. No two runs look the same.
The thin floating ledges and plank stairs are gone.
Wall climbing lasts 3 seconds, up from 2.

Co-op map: your partner shows in cyan with a line and arrow pointing to them, including how far up or down they are. In-game, an arrow at the screen edge always points to your partner when they're off screen.

[B] is now Quick-treat. It picks the best fix for your worst problem: a tourniquet for an arterial bleed, a dressing or stitches for bleeding, forceps for a fragment, a splint for a broken bone, popping a dislocated joint back in, a transfusion, antibiotics, antiseptic, painkillers or anti-rad. The hotbar shows what it will do next.
Your crosshair, the heavy-attack charge ring and bar, and the progress bars now use your Vespa's colour.
Lunge now needs a FULL wind-up (when the bar flashes) before you press RMB.

log.title: Real standoffs, speech bubbles, new sound
changes: Standoffs work properly now. The two raiders turn to face you and talk, and each choice plays out:
• Hand over your meds: they take them and walk off into the dark. The option is greyed out if you have none.
• Talk them down: if it works they lower their weapons and leave. If not, they attack.
• Fight: they attack, but you get a moment to strike first.

When someone talks, it now appears in a speech bubble over their own head, with their name: town folk, survivors, traders, doctors and raiders. Hostile people shout when they spot you, executioners say something before the blow, and standoff crews do their talking too.

Sound rework: hits, footsteps, landings, swings, gunshots, explosions, bone cracks, blocks and parries, doors and crates, water, breathing, menus and more are rebuilt from softer, filtered noise with real thumps and metal rings. Everything plays through a light cave reverb and a compressor, and each sound varies slightly every time. Nothing beeps like a chiptune any more.

log.title: Rolls, lunges, puffy packs
changes: Dash is now a real combat roll. You dive forward, tuck into a ball, roll across the ground and come up on your feet. You're untouchable for the first 0.24s.

Lunge has a new input: hold LMB until your wind-up is full, then press RMB. You throw your weight forward into a heavy strike. It travels much less distance than before and has a 2.6s cooldown plus a longer recovery. Sprinting or dashing no longer triggers it by accident.
Enemy lunges also travel less distance.
Searching anything now has an animation. You kneel at the container, turn to face it, and dig through it with both hands while dust kicks up.
Backpacks look like backpacks: rounded and stuffed, with a bedroll on top, a front pocket, a buckle and a shoulder strap. Bigger packs bulge more.
Every backpack and outfit has an icon again in the Gear Rack and the Quartermaster. Packs and outfits without their own art get a matching pixel icon in their colours.
In co-op, your partner's rolls, searching and out-of-breath panting now show on your screen too.

log.title: Shared water, party health bars
changes: Co-op: only the host runs the water, lava and honey flow now. The host streams every changed cell near your partner several times a second, so both screens show the same pools, floods and waterfalls.
Saves keep liquid exactly as you left it: flooded holes, drained pools and spent springs all come back when you load. They also come back when the host reloads in co-op.

Party health in co-op: your partner's card sits under your portrait. It shows health, blood and stamina bars, how far away they are (left/right or meters up/down), and their worst problems (bleeding rate, broken bones, DOWN — revive!, DEAD). A raised brood minion shows its HP there too.
Your partner also has a name tag and health bar floating over their head. It turns red when they're down.

log.title: Bodies, blood and the deep
changes: Combat rework: Q dashes through attacks (with i-frames, afterimages and a whoosh). Right-click raises a guard. Raise it just before a hit to PARRY, which staggers the attacker; holding it blocks for stamina. Heavy blows break guards. A quick right-click tap pokes with your weapon, and attacking while sprinting or right after a dash LUNGES for 30% more damage. Throwable cycling moved to T.

Enemies now telegraph their swings, raise their own guards, lunge at you, and back off to recover. Hitting them while they recover deals 30% more damage. Heavy hits land with real weight: hit-stop, screen shake, sparks and knockdowns.

Full ragdolls: explosions, hard falls, heavy blows and blackouts throw bodies limp. When they settle, they get back up. Arms and legs bend independently and knees buckle on hard landings. Arms are longer and reach out to poke.
Waking up from a knockdown is much easier: about 6 presses, or just hold SPACE.
Dislocations: blunt hits, falls and big knockdowns can pop a joint out. The limb barely works until you pop it back in (Anatomy → Procedures). That's free but agonising, and it can slip.
Self-amputation: with a saw, axe, cleaver, machete or even a knife, you can take off a limb (Anatomy → Procedures). This removes every wound and infection on it. Put a tourniquet on first.

Prosthetics in Worn / Average / Pristine tiers: peg legs, hook arms, scrap-metal arms and legs, Saw-Blade Arms (fight unarmed with a spinning saw), and very rare Artificer limbs that work better than flesh. Most give 50-80% function. Fit them in Anatomy.
New Grappling Hook item: press Z to fire it at the rock above and reel yourself up. Hold a direction to swing, S to let out rope, and jump or Z to let go.
Liquids now flow: water, lava and honey pour down shafts, spread, stack and flood the holes you dig. Springs pour from cave ceilings. Water and lava meeting cool into rock.

New animations: swimming strokes, doubled-over panting when out of stamina, and proper self-treatment. You wrap bandages, haul on tourniquets, stitch, splint, saw, and sit down to work on a leg. Each has its own sound.
Four new deep biomes past the Magma Abyss: Hive Warrens (1300m, sticky honey), Drowned Abyss (1600m, flooding), Bone Ossuary (1900m) and The Nectar Heart (2300m).

10 new enemies: Acid Spitter, Hulking Brute, Hive Swarmling (packs), Hive Warden, Drowned Diver, Ossuary Revenant, Wailing Mourner, Skulker (near-invisible), Bloated Host (bursts into spores) and Nectar Knight. Enemies can also spawn as Armoured, Frenzied, Hulking, Veteran or Nectar-Touched variants.
The Vespa burst no longer latches. Press E on someone close to SWALLOW them whole for big XP and extra seconds.

12 new Vespa gifts: Emergency Molt, Brood Shield, Barbed Strikes, Hive Resonance, Adrenal Sac, Chitin Bulwark, Spring Tendons, Gorging Gut, Wax Glands, Quill Burst, Gill Slits and Echo Sense. Gift order is random every run, but your first gifts are modest and the run-defining ones only show up later.

30 new armour pieces in regional sets: Mosshide, Spelunker, Nomad, Ruin-Guard, Furclad, Ice-Cutter, Shardplate, Prism, Obsidian, Firewalker, Chitin, Diver, Ossuary and Workshop. Some keep you warm or cool, block radiation or gas, or soften falls.

10 utility pieces in four new slots (hands, feet, belt, charm): Hiking Boots (cling to walls), Running Shoes, Climbing Gloves, Weighted Knuckle Gloves, a Canteen Belt (thirst -40%), a Larder Pouch (hunger -40%), a Load-Bearing Harness, a Medic's Armband, Night-Eye Goggles and a Lucky Rabbit's Foot.
20 new backpacks and outfits. The Gear Rack is now a tabbed card grid with All / Owned / Locked filters, a live preview and a stats panel, and you can buy locked items right there.

Medical Cabinets now only appear inside medical tents, and they stock prosthetics and surgical gear. Lockers stand inside little sheds. 30 new region-themed containers: ore carts, sarcophagi, frozen climbers, specimen cases, wax cells, sea-chests, ossuary boxes and more.
Fixes: the Paramedic pack's half-weight medical bonus now actually works. Guard-post enemies no longer block every hit. Taking off gear no longer freezes the game.

log.title: Real weapon models
changes: Every weapon now has its own pixel model in your hands. These are drawn pixel-by-pixel and turn with your aim without blurring.

Melee weapons: the Rock Hammer has a hammer face and pick, the Ice Axe and Fire Axe have proper heads, the pickaxe has a curved double pick, and the sledgehammer has a big block head. The crowbar has a hooked claw, the spear has a leaf-shaped tip, and the knife, machete, cleaver, lead pipe, riot baton and flint dagger each have their own look.
Guns get their own shapes too: pistol, revolver, SMG, battle rifle, pump shotgun, and a scoped .50 hunting rifle, with wooden stocks behind the hand.

log.title: Fairer depths, rewarding fights
changes: Fewer enemies the deeper you go. Each level now has at most 2 hostiles above 300m and at most 3 below, instead of up to 6. The count grows slowly with depth, troglodyte packs are rarer, and ambushes are smaller and less frequent.
Every enemy now drops Silver, a new currency all traders accept. Tougher foes and deeper levels drop more.

Enemies also have a good chance to carry supplies like bandages, painkillers, water, food, lantern oil, tape or ammo. The toughest ones (Stalkers, Burrowers, Rival Hosts, Expedition soldiers) sometimes carry Relic Nectar.
Kills now give XP based on how dangerous the enemy was and how deep you are, shown as a '+XP' pop-up. Kill XP counts toward your end-of-run total.

log.title: Nectar & strain gifts
changes: Relic flowers are easier to find. Each one has a pulsing golden ring and rising motes, and a soft chime that gets louder and faster as you get close, even from the level above or below.
Drinking nectar now plays an animation: golden light spirals into your eyes, you sink to a crouch for a moment, time slows and a flash goes off.
Infestation rises much more gently. One nectar adds about 4–5% instead of ~10%, and lifetime nectars barely count.

13 new strain gifts. Each Vespa strain has its own signature gifts that only it can awaken with nectar: 1 for Common, 2 for Uncommon and Rare, 3 for Epic and Legendary, 4 for Mythical and Secret. The gifts are Honeyed Flesh, Drone Swarm, Blood Frenzy, Limb Carapace, Locust Legs, Rot Breath, Hive Mind, Honey Blood, Ember Glands, Frost Coat, Phantom Step, Royal Command and Spined Hide.
The Status tab lists your strain's gifts, with ✦ for ones you've awakened and ◇ for ones you haven't yet.

Lodged fragments: no forceps? Dig them out with a knife, cleaver, shiv, machete, lockpick, crowbar, spear, pickaxe, axe or a piece of scrap. It hurts more and gets the wound dirtier. Each tool has a chance to slip; on success every fragment in that body part comes out.

log.title: Selling, calmer boxes, shared events
changes: Traders now buy. The trade window has a Sell column listing your items, each with what the trader will pay (about 40% of shop price, less for used-up or worn gear). Selling gives you credit you can spend there or at any other trader this run.
Boxes behave. Crates and barrels settle and stay put instead of trembling or ping-ponging. Walking into them nudges them gently, and town folk no longer shove them around.

Props only hurt when they really hit you: something thrown, falling, blasted by an explosion, or falling rock. A box being pushed or jittering never deals damage, and neither do props being synced in co-op.

Co-op: world events are shared. The host rolls cave-ins, blackouts, gas, distress beacons and ambushes for both of you, aimed at either player. Blackouts darken both screens, and you get a log line when something hits your partner's level.

log.title: Google cloud saves
changes: New "Sign in with Google" button on the title screen, under Save Slots and Settings. Your saves (all 3 slots and your settings) are backed up to a private folder in your Google Drive that only this game can see.
While you're signed in, every save is backed up automatically. If your Google account already has a save, you choose whether to load the cloud copy or keep this device's save.
Click the button while signed in to back up now, load from the cloud, or sign out. Signing out never deletes anything on this device.

log.title: No more ropes
changes: Ropes are gone. Every way down is now a natural path: winding sloped tunnels and collapsed caverns with stair-step ledges. Every level is guaranteed at least one way down, and towns lead on through a winding stair cut into the floor.

Respawn sound: when the Vespa takes a new host (a new run, or a new host after dying in co-op), you hear a wet gasp, a rising hive-shimmer and the new host's first heartbeats. Co-op re-hosting also gets a flash of glow.

Inventory rebalance: the starting rucksack is now a 10×4 grid (40 cells), down from 60. Better backpacks now clearly add room: Paramedic and Hauling Rig 10×5, Brass 10×6, Expedition Frame 10×7, Crystal Duffel 10×8. Every 2 ranks of Pack Mule or Organized Packing add another row. The Gear Rack shows each pack's grid size and cell count.

log.title: Safe towns
changes: Towns are true safe havens. Hostiles never spawn on a town floor, and any that fall or wander in vanish. Enemies chasing you stop the moment you reach a town, and an enemy standing over you for a finisher backs off.

log.title: Cleaner title screen
changes: The honey cursor now always shows on the title screen and menus, not only when you hover a button.
Removed the big winch lift and the dark cliff on the right of the title screen. The cave scene is now centered, with the warm glow rising from below.

log.title: Grid inventory
changes: Tarkov-style grid inventory. Items now take up space by size: knives 2×1, splints and canteens 1×2, pistols 2×1, SMGs 3×2, rifles and shotguns 5×2, sledgehammers 4×2, spears 5×1, helmets 2×2 and body armor 3×3. Small stuff is 1×1.
Drag items to rearrange your pack. Press R while dragging to rotate. A green outline shows where it fits and red shows where it doesn't. Double-click to equip, wear, eat, drink or use.
New items are packed in automatically, rotating them if that's the only way they fit. If there's no room, you'll be told to make space.
Long weapons are drawn lengthwise in their cells, and each item category has its own background tint.
The loot screen shows your pack as a grid. Click an item to stash it in the container, or drag to rearrange.
Bigger packs to make up for it: the starting rucksack is a 10×6 grid (60 cells), and bigger backpacks and skill bonuses add more rows. Every pack also carries 6kg more.
Old saves are re-packed into the grid automatically, and anything that doesn't fit is dropped in a bag at your feet.

log.title: Bigger packs
changes: Every backpack holds 8 more items. The starting rucksack now has 20 slots instead of 12, and skill and pack bonuses stack on top.

log.title: Fight back
changes: Knocked down? Mash Space or click to fight back. If an enemy stands over you for the finisher, you now have about 4 seconds to throw them off. Each press also pushes their swing back. Breaking free stuns everyone nearby and gives you a few seconds of second wind so you don't black out again straight away.

Co-op: when your partner dies, walk over their corpse and press E to raise it as a brood minion. It costs you a little blood. The dead player steers the minion ([A/D] move, [Space] hop, [LMB] bite) while their Vespa waits for a new host. Minions are weak and burst after a few hits, but their kills count as Vespa kills.
Co-op: corpses you drag now move on your partner's screen too.
Double-tap Crouch to go fully prone and stay down. Double-tap again, jump or sprint to get up.
You can chip away at any rock with any weapon, or your bare hands, to dig out of tight spots. Pickaxes are still much faster. Rock now shows cracks that spread as it takes damage.
Your hits knock people back properly and briefly loosen their footing.
Enemies no longer trade blows nonstop. They back off after each swing, hold at the edge of their reach while they recover, and take turns instead of all swinging at once.
Enemies' weapons no longer hurt you while they're winding up, and they can't hit you while you're down except with the finisher.
Bones break far less easily. Blunt hits need real force to fracture, falls are much gentler (you take less damage and land safely from higher up), and big falls rarely break both legs.
New Strength skills: Hauler (+3kg carry per rank, and heavy loads slow you less) and Organized Packing (+1 inventory slot per rank, and stacks hold 25% more).
The Status tab now shows your Vespa strain: its name, rarity, what it does, and any nectar gifts you've awakened.
Loot screen: your pack is on the left and the container is on the right.

log.title: Sharp text
changes: The captions in the host-taking cutscene are now sharp, readable text instead of blurry canvas text. The same fix applies to the lift's LOWERING label and the Vespa burst countdown.

log.title: Deeper detail
changes: New cave backgrounds: chunky shaded rock blocks that scroll slower than the foreground for depth. Each biome adds its own touches: hanging vines and moss in the Grotto, sediment bands in the desert, frost cracks in the ice, glowing crystal veins and glints, and molten cracks in the Magma Abyss.
Each weapon now swings differently. Batons and fists are quick and short; machetes sweep wide; fire axes and sledgehammers are slow and heavy; spears lunge far.

Enemy types are easier to tell apart at a glance. Troglodytes, Stalkers, Burrowers and Addicts crouch forward when they move. Stalkers have long bone claws and Troglodytes have short ones. Burrowers have armored shell plates and mandibles. Husks are covered in fungus. Addicts have glowing nectar veins.
Town folk and wounded survivors now take fall damage too.
The Cave Spear recipe no longer needs a Rock Hammer: Flint Dagger + 2 Scrap + 2 Duct Tape.

log.title: Into the Deep — the big overhaul
changes: Each new host now starts with a short cutscene: a spark of hive-light falls down the shaft, circles the caver, and pours in through the eyes. Click or press Space to skip.

Run grades: the death screen grades your run from F to S. It shows a score breakdown (depth, kills, Vespa kills, survivors helped, towns reached, nectar gifts, time alive) and how many skill points you earned. Grades S, A, B and C give 3, 2, 1 and 1 bonus skill points.

Caves are more winding, with several ways down. Sloped tunnels snake through the rock into the next band and carry on as stair-step ledges. Collapsed caverns have switchback ledges. Ceilings are lower and wavier, some ledges are solid rock you can climb onto, and ropes are now rare.

30 Vespa strains in six tiers: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythical. Each host rolls one, which sets its eye color, glow and a passive bonus, and higher tiers are stronger. There are also 3 Secret strains, which you can only get from relic flowers or from Royal Jelly dropped by rival hosts.

Vespa burst: a screech, a blinding flash and a ring of glowing ichor, then a wet retraction when it ends. Press Space to leap toward the cursor and latch onto an enemy, stabbing them with tendrils. Vespa kills are worth +35 XP each.

New enemies: Feral Nectar-Addicts, Husked Spelunkers, Pale Troglodytes (which hunt in packs), Blind Cave Stalkers (which hunt by sound, so crouch-walk past them), Chitinous Burrowers (armored, and they dig through rock to reach you), Rival Parasite Hosts (violet eyes) and Deranged Expeditions. Each biome has its own mix, and only humans spawn near the surface.

Enemies wind up before every swing so you can read and dodge it. Heavy hits stagger them. If you get knocked out, an enemy can stand over you and finish you with one blow. Enemies and NPCs now take fall damage too.
+20% player damage. Weapons outreach fists and claws. Every heavy attack is now an overhead chop or slam, fists included. When a gun runs dry, you pistol-whip or rifle-butt instead.
New melee weapons: Machete, Fire Axe, Sledgehammer, Cave Spear (the longest reach), Lead Pipe, Riot Baton and Butcher Knife. Heavy blades can take limbs off.

New guns: .357 Revolver, Mine SMG (hold to fire), Pump Shotgun (7 pellets) and .50 Hunting Rifle. Caliber now scales recoil, sound, penetration, how hard targets are shoved and staggered, and how often limbs are torn off.

Armor sets: Leather, Tactical (Kevlar), Scrap Plate, Steel Riot and Hazmat. Each has different resistances per damage type, plus its own weight and speed cost. A full Hazmat set blocks gas and most radiation.

Bleeding rebalance: normal hits cause lighter wounds, and heavy bleeding comes from big hits, high calibers and heavy blades. Minor and moderate wounds clot on their own much faster. Bandages and rags press shut minor bleeds and cut worse ones down hard. Dirty rags work as dressings but raise infection risk.
Cave water: stand in it and press E to drink. Clear water is safe, but murky water can make you sick. Hold Crouch and press E to wash dirty rags into clean ones (clear water only).
The health card shows how many injuries are still untreated, and the treatment bar shows % done and how many injuries are left. Starving or dehydrated hosts also slow down.

Co-op: dropped items land in a bag your partner can see and pick up. Physics props now sync between players, including when one of you drags them. Press E next to your partner to triage their body parts with your supplies, or revive them if they're unconscious. You both see the progress bar.
30 new traits: positive, negative and trade-offs such as Glass Cannon, Heavyset, Bruiser and Pack Mule.
New descent cutscene: the cage drops down a rock shaft, with sparks off the guide rails, a swinging lantern lighting the hosts inside, and a honey progress bar.

Base Camp is now a modern field station with a sofa, desk terminal, fridge, shelves, plants, a generator and a neon hive sign. Towns got tables and furniture too. Crates, lockers, strongboxes and bags have more detail.
The depth meter is back in the top-left as a progress bar toward the next town.
New settings: UI scale and Text size.

log.title: Clean faces & full hair
changes: Portraits: faces are now just clean skin. Scars, freckles, stubble specks, age lines, jaw stripes, earrings and the random neck pixels are gone.
Blush only shows on women now.

Every hairstyle now covers the whole scalp and both sides of the head, in portraits and in-game, so nobody has the 'hood' look anymore. Side hair sits outside the face edge instead of stepping in over the cheeks.
Hair has strand shading instead of flat color.

20 new hairstyles: pompadour, side part, crop, mullet, topknot, emo, tall spikes, slick-back, lob, shag, layered, half-up, side braid, bangs bob, long curls, pigtails, locs, bowl cut, tousled, and an ahoge cut.
Women have a more feminine in-game silhouette (bust, waist and hips) that every shirt and armor follows.
Swimming: you can stroke upward from any depth and haul yourself out of flooded pits onto a ledge.
Wall climbing: hold W against a rock face to latch on and climb for up to 2 seconds, then pull yourself over the edge.
New arm-over-arm crawl animation, with legs dragging limp when they're broken or gone.

log.title: Honey cursor & new Status tab
changes: Custom pixel cursors: a honey arrow on menus, a pointing hand over anything clickable, and a new honey reticle in-game. With guns it's four ticks that spread when you're shaky or just fired. With melee it's a small cross with a ring that fills while you charge a heavy attack.

Status tab restyled in the game's amber and wax look: a host header with portrait and a striped Vespa hold meter, a honey heartbeat monitor, wax-edged stat cards, honey-gradient organ bars and rounded condition chips.

log.title: Heavy attacks, lighter crates, bigger skill web
changes: Hold the attack button to wind up a heavy attack (a bar fills over your head), then release for up to 2.1x damage, a bigger swing, harder knockback and a short hit-stop. A quick click is still a fast strike.
Scroll the mouse wheel to cycle through your weapons and tools (fists included). A quick picker shows what you're holding.
Object weight now comes from size and material: crates are easy to lift and toss, barrels a bit heavier, rocks and rubble dense. Your strength makes dragging easier.
10 new skills (2-3 per branch): Clotting, Vitality, Parkour, Sprinter, Nimble Fingers, Lanternwright, Composure, Silver Tongue, Brawler and Pack Mule.
Skill web: branches stay closed until you click one, which zooms in on just that branch. Clicking a cell selects it and shows a Confirm upgrade button, so you never spend a point by accident.

log.title: Blood & Physics
changes: Physics melee: your melee weapon (or fists) is held toward your cursor all the time. Damage comes from how fast the blade or head is actually moving, so whipping the mouse across someone hurts. Click to strike: knives, shivs and fists thrust, heavier weapons do a big overhead swing. Heavy weapons swing slower but hit harder, and blunt ones bounce off on impact. Enemies fight the same way.

Bullets are real projectiles: they travel, drop a little, punch through bodies, ricochet off rock at shallow angles, shove ragdolls and loose objects, and spray blood out the exit side. Muzzle flashes and ejected casings too.

Gore (scales with the Gore setting): limbs get cut, blown or shot off and fly around as physics objects with bone stumps, heads can come off, torsos spill intestines and organs (heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, stomach) that flop and bleed, bodies get stained where they were hit, and corpses keep bleeding into growing pools. Losing a leg puts you on the ground, losing an arm cripples your swing. Explosions tear people apart, and you can hack at or shoot corpses.
Faster combat: shorter melee cooldowns, faster gun fire and reloads, and enemies aim and fire sooner.
Movement: walking is about 50% faster and running is a real feature (about 2x walking speed). Hold Shift or double-tap a direction to run, and running drains stamina more slowly.
New animations: proper walk and run cycles with planted steps, bending knees and counter-swinging arms. Running leans forward with pumping arms and kicks up dust, and landings squash.

log.title: Honeycomb skill web
changes: Skill web redesigned as a honeycomb: wax cells fill with dripping honey as you unlock ranks, category cells fill up with honey too, the hub is now the striped Vespa, and the colors are warm cave tones. Labels no longer overlap and the big hexes no longer cover each other.
The depth meter now sits under your portrait, and its text no longer clips into the bar.
Every host's portrait gets its own background color.

Glass shards no longer appear all over the caves (none in the Mossy Grotto, rare patches in the Crystal Depths). The ones that remain are bright, outlined, glinting and lit, so you can see them coming.

log.title: Taller, more detailed characters
changes: Every human is now drawn taller with more pixels, closer to People Playground proportions: a square head with nose, eye and brow, a longer torso with a belt, slim outlined arms and legs, hands and boots. Hair, beards, helmets, masks, backpacks and weapons were redrawn to match.

log.title: Wall parkour, lanterns & rebindable keys
changes: Every keybind can be changed in Settings: click a key, press the new one (Del clears, Esc cancels). Each action has two slots and a reset button. On-screen hints update to match.
Volume sliders now use the game's honey colors and follow the selected UI theme.
Hex menu rebuilt: the hexes no longer overlap and every button's name is printed inside it.
Wall parkour: hold toward a wall in mid-air to slide down it, press Jump to kick off the other way, and Sprint+Jump into a wall to boost up it (twice per jump). You can chain wall jumps up shafts.
The flashlight is now a small oil lantern hanging at your waist. It sways as you move and lights all around you instead of a cone. Batteries are now Lantern Oil.
Every human now carries a waist lantern: raiders, soldiers, traders and townsfolk (the cave-mad wretches don't). You can see them coming, and they light you up too.
Fall damage reduced by 30%.

log.title: Centered title screen
changes: The logo and main menu are now centered on every screen width, including ultrawide.

log.title: The Vespa
changes: New lore: you are a Vespa, a parasite from an interstellar hive mind, riding human hosts deeper and deeper into the caves. That's why every host is a random new person.
Full prologue cutscene on your first game (replay it from the title screen). Click or Space to advance, Esc to skip.
Your host's eyes glow gold and leave a fading trail. The glow cuts through total darkness so you always know which one is you.

Relic flowers grow deeper down. Their nectar awakens one of 8 Vespa gifts: Overclocked Heart, Chitin Plating, Compound Sight, Stinger Lash, Wing Buds (glide), Hive Pulse [X], Amber Blood and Mandibles.
When your host dies, the Vespa bursts out as a tendril-lashing goo for 10 seconds. Take them with you.
No more extraction. A town waits every 250m with an inn bed (rest & save), a doctor, a trader, a well, a workbench and a Deep Post that sends your loot up to Base Camp.

Online co-op: pick 'Descend with a partner' at the lift, share a 5-letter room code and go down together. Shared cave and enemies. Each player keeps their own save, and reloading reconnects automatically. In co-op a dead player's Vespa drifts to their partner and takes a new host.
Save slots (3) and autosave: every few seconds, when you rest, and whenever you close or reload the page. Reloading drops you right back where you were.
Destructible terrain: dig through rock with a Pickaxe, Ice Axe or Rock Hammer (aim at the rock and click). Dynamite blows holes in walls. Both can be found, bought and crafted.
Ropes: jump off them any time, climb about 60% faster, and Shift+S slides down fast. Press W mid-air to grab one.
Walking into a low gap now drops you into a crawl automatically, so crawlspaces stop snagging you.
Objects have real weight: heavy crates fall hard, drag slowly and can't be lifted high. Crates no longer launch themselves at you or do big damage. Dragged objects barely hurt.
Guns hit harder (pistol 46, rifle 84) and headshots deal 1.5x.
Generative background music for the title, prologue, Base Camp, each biome, towns and the death burst. The ambient drone is gone.
New colored anime-style pixel portraits that blink, plus 30+ hairstyles across men and women.
Redesigned title screen with a clear menu: Continue/New Game, Save Slots, Settings, then Prologue, Run Archive and Update Log.
Modern glassy HUD: new bottom-left vitals card, hotbar, depth gauge and portrait card.
7 UI themes in Settings (Honey, Abyss Blue, Moss, Ember, Amethyst, Hive Contrast, Bone & Ink) and new rounded volume sliders.
Livelier caves: fireflies, sand motes, snow, crystal glints and embers drift around. Biomes are a bit less dark, and the grotto has far fewer spores.
Backpacks, outfits and all new items now use Pixel Atlas icons.

log.title: Into the Caves
changes: Nectar's End is now a cave-diving game: organic caves with uneven floors, stalactites, rock ledges, ropes down, risky open pits and crawlspaces.

Five cave biomes, each with a perk and a challenge: Mossy Grotto (forage mushrooms & herbs / spores, damp wounds), Sunscorched Sandstone (dry air, ruins & prickly pears / heat & sinking sand), Frozen Hollows (cold slows bleeding, fresh water / hypothermia, slippery ice, falling icicles), Crystal Depths (glowing crystals, Crystal Shards / crystal radiation, shard floors) and Magma Abyss (no cold, richest caches / heat, lava, steam vents).
Walk up small cave steps automatically.
New items: Cave Mushroom, Healing Herb, Prickly Pear, Glowcap (throwable light), Rock; cave-themed weapons and gear.
All item, menu and skill icons replaced with CC0 Pixel Atlas sprites.
Base Camp lobby, winch lifts, expedition camps, triage tents, mine storerooms and research outposts.
New cave title screen.

log.title: Update notifications & update log
changes: New versions now announce themselves with a popup: Update now, or it auto-updates after a countdown.
Added this Update Log (title screen, Settings, and the update popup).
"What's new" opens automatically the first time you load a new version.
Pain rebalanced: wounds hurt less constantly, threshold raised to 60.

log.title: First playable build
changes: Title screen, Staging Lobby with Skill Terminal, Gear Locker, Quartermaster and Survivor Dossier.
Random human survivor every run: name, age, occupation, traits and looks.
Endless descent through four biomes with a depth meter and extraction elevators every 250m.
Limb-by-limb anatomy, organs, bleeding, fractures, infection, pain and blackouts; triage by body part.
Loose verlet physics: ragdolls, props, debris, throwables, right-click dragging.
Hex menu (M), fading-ink portrait, hex skill web, crafting, map, journal, cemetery.
Ultrawide support up to 32:9.
